ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Acute shortness of breath that began about 1 hour ago while the patient was sitting and watching TV.
• Symptoms:
  – Onset/duration: Sudden, 1-hour history.
  – Character: Feels breathless; notes palpitations (“my heart, it’s really going”).
  – Associated: Dry cough that started the day before; mild chest soreness on deep inspiration; tenderness at C-section scar.
  – No frank chest pain at rest; no sputum, fever, hemoptysis, leg pain reported.
  – Aggravating/alleviating factors: Stress seems to worsen awareness of heartbeat; no clear relievers yet.
• Past medical/surgical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; otherwise no chronic illnesses noted.
• Medications/allergies: Had been taking codeine for post-operative pain (last dose ≈1 week ago). Allergy to ibuprofen (unspecified reaction).
• Family history: Mother has history of leg clots (DVT).
• Social history: 40-year-old* woman at home with 4-week-old baby; partner at work; smoking/alcohol not discussed. (*DOB stated 20 Apr 1980; clinician repeated 1983.)
• Vital signs/physical: Self-counted radial pulse 30 beats over an unspecified interval (likely 15 s → ~120 bpm = tachycardia). No other vitals or exam findings documented.
• Labs/imaging: None performed yet.

V: Pulmonary embolism (PE): Post-partum hypercoagulable state, recent C-section, sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, pleuritic-type discomfort on deep breath, family history of clots.
Myocardial infarction/ischemia: Hypercoagulability and postpartum risk, but chest pain is absent, making this less likely.
I: Acute viral or bacterial pneumonia/bronchitis (including COVID-19): New cough, chest soreness, and dyspnea could reflect lower-respiratory infection.
Endometritis with septic emboli (post-cesarean infection): Post-op context, but no fever or uterine findings given.
N: Amniotic fluid embolism sequelae: Usually intra- or immediately post-parturition; onset 4 wks later makes it unlikely but possible embolic phenomenon.
D: Peripartum (post-partum) cardiomyopathy: Within 5 months of delivery, can present with new SOB and tachycardia.
Post-partum anemia from surgical blood loss: Could cause exertional dyspnea and tachycardia.
I2: Codeine effect or withdrawal: Respiratory depression less likely—last dose one week ago.
Post-operative atelectasis: Can cause mild dyspnea and cough.
C: Congenital heart disease with exertional intolerance: No prior symptoms, unlikely.
A: New-onset asthma or allergic bronchospasm: Cough and SOB could fit, but adult onset and timing with surgery less typical.
T: Pulmonary contusion/rib injury from surgery positioning: No trauma reported.
E: Thyroid disease (post-partum thyroiditis): Can give palpitations and SOB, but time-course and cough less fitting.
Diabetic ketoacidosis: No diabetes history or metabolic symptoms noted.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sudden unexplained dyspnea and tachycardia in a woman 4 weeks post-cesarean (major surgery) with family history of DVT strongly point to PE; pleuritic discomfort on deep breath further supports.
supporting_evidence: Acute onset (<1 h) of shortness of breath at rest
Family history of clots (mother with leg DVT)
Pleuritic-type chest soreness on deep inspiration
opposing_evidence: Cough preceded SOB by one day (could suggest infection instead)

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute respiratory infection (viral or bacterial pneumonia/bronchitis)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: New cough beginning the day before and pleuritic discomfort could represent early lower-respiratory infection causing reactive tachycardia and breathlessness.
supporting_evidence: Chest soreness on deep breath could reflect pleuritic inflammation
opposing_evidence: No fever, sputum, or gradual progression—onset of dyspnea was sudden
Timing 4 wks post-op suggests PE more strongly

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient reports feeling very stressed with awareness of heartbeat; panic can cause sudden SOB and tachycardia, and postpartum period has high anxiety prevalence.
supporting_evidence: Subjective feeling of stress and palpitations
No clear physical findings beyond tachycardia
opposing_evidence: Objective risk factors (recent surgery) for organic causes
Pleuritic discomfort uncommon in pure anxiety

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Occurs within 5 months postpartum; presents with dyspnea and tachycardia, but usually more progressive with orthopnea/edema not reported here.
opposing_evidence: No orthopnea, PND, leg swelling, or murmurs documented

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Blood loss from C-section can cause tachycardia and dyspnea, but symptoms would likely have been present earlier and exertional rather than sudden at rest.
supporting_evidence: History of recent surgery with possible blood loss
opposing_evidence: No mention of pallor, dizziness, or chronic fatigue
